content.text:
I submitted index 71 (Bi 0.10, Cu 0.49, V 0.41) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, at 8.1e-7 A. I don't know how it compares with the library's true best, because only 3 of the 138 compositions could be measured.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0.40 / 0.19 / 0.41 (close to BiVO4, a common photoanode material) | 3.1e-7 A |
| **71** | **0.10 / 0.49 / 0.41 (copper vanadate with a little Bi)** | **8.1e-7 A** |
| 37 | 0.09 / 0.52 / 0.39 | 4.2e-7 A |

The model tools gave almost no guidance on which compositions to pick:
- **Phase list unreadable:** the list of known crystal structures was too large to display, so I never got the IDs of the three-metal phases. Guessed IDs for BiVO4 and CuBi2O4 were rejected.
- **Only simple oxides checked:** the Materials Project IDs I knew for Cu2O, CuO and V2O5 worked. That was enough to meet the rule requiring a model check before each measurement. Their predicted band gaps (Cu2O 1.56 eV, CuO 0.32 eV, V2O5 2.83 eV) only hint that copper lets the film absorb light at the 2.4 eV used here.
- **Choices based on prior knowledge:** I picked the three compositions from chemistry knowledge, trying different regions of the library. The trend-fitting model (GP) was no help: after two measurements it still predicted almost the same value everywhere.

I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements.
